hook.headline: Your AI Board of Directors
hook.p1: Every important decision in business is made by a group of advisors — not one. A board of directors, a council of experts, a panel of specialists. Each brings a different lens, challenges the others' assumptions, and helps arrive at a stronger conclusion.
hook.p2: DebateKit brings this same principle to AI. Instead of asking one model and hoping for the best, you convene a council of AI models that debate, challenge, and build on each other's reasoning before delivering a synthesized answer.

problem.headline: The Single-Model
problem.label: The Problem
problem.p1: When you ask a question to ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini, you get one perspective. That perspective might be brilliant — or it might have blind spots. There's no way to know, because there's no one challenging it.
problem.p2: Every language model has systematic biases shaped by its training data and alignment process. One model might over-index on caution while another misses regulatory nuance. One excels at quantitative analysis but underweights human factors. You'd never make a major business decision by asking a single advisor — why do it with AI?
problem.p3: The problem isn't that any one model is bad — it's that you're relying on a single point of failure for important decisions.

insight.headline: What If They Could
insight.label: The Insight
insight.p1: DebateKit implements sequential multi-model deliberation. Here's what that means: when you ask a question, it doesn't go to one model — it goes to a council of models. You choose which ones, or let auto mode pick the best combination.
insight.p2: Each model takes a turn. But crucially, each one sees what the previous models said. They challenge, extend, and reframe each other's reasoning. This isn't parallel generation — it's a structured debate.
insight.p3: At the end, a moderator model reads the entire deliberation and produces a final synthesis — capturing the strongest arguments, resolving conflicts, and presenting a cohesive answer that no single model could have produced alone.
insight.step1Desc: You type a question or paste a problem — anything from an investment memo to a clinical assessment to a strategic decision.
insight.step2Desc: Multiple AI models take turns responding. Each sees what came before — challenging, extending, and reframing the conversation.
insight.step3Desc: A moderator reads the full deliberation and distills it into one cohesive answer with the strongest reasoning from all sides.

evidence.headline: Backed by
evidence.label: Evidence
evidence.p1: This isn't a gimmick or a prompt engineering trick. Multi-model deliberation is a well-studied technique backed by peer-reviewed research from leading AI labs.
evidence.p2: At ICML 2024, researchers demonstrated that multi-model debate produces answers that are 28% more accurate than single-model responses. A joint study by MIT and Google DeepMind showed 15% improvement in reasoning quality — models genuinely catch and correct each other's mistakes.
evidence.p3: Four peer-reviewed papers across ICML, NeurIPS, and ICLR have validated this approach. The research comes from Anthropic, Google DeepMind, MIT, and Stanford.

mcp.label: MCP Integration
mcp.headline: Works Inside Your
mcp.p1: DebateKit runs as an MCP server inside Claude Code, Cursor, and any MCP-compatible client. Your agent invokes the council when the stakes are high — no tab-switching, no copy-paste.
mcp.mode1Desc: Agent plans an approach. Council stress-tests it before code is written.
mcp.mode2Desc: Agent hits a fork. Council debates the tradeoffs and picks a path.
mcp.mode3Desc: Full deliberation. Multiple models argue, then a moderator synthesizes the verdict.

platforms.headline: Works Where You
platforms.label: Platforms
platforms.p1: DebateKit isn't just a web app. It's available as an MCP server for Claude Code and Cursor, a ChatGPT plugin, a Slack and Telegram bot, a Zapier integration, and a direct API. Wherever you make decisions, DebateKit can be there.

demo.headline: See It
demo.label: Demo
demo.p1: This is what a DebateKit debate actually looks like. Multiple models. One question. A structured deliberation that arrives at a better answer than any single model could produce.

worthIt.headline: Why It's
worthIt.label: The ROI Argument
worthIt.p1: Multi-model costs more tokens. But that's pennies compared to the cost of a bad decision.
worthIt.card1Desc: per debate. That's a board of advisors for the price of a coffee. One bad hire costs $50K. One wrong strategic call costs a quarter. This costs fifteen cents.
worthIt.card2Desc: lost to bad operational decisions (Gartner). Every executive knows the feeling — a decision that looked right until it wasn't. A second opinion would have caught it.
worthIt.card3Desc: across tasks (MIT, ICML 2024 Best Paper). Not marginally better — fundamentally different. Models catch each other's blind spots the way good advisors do.
worthIt.footer: For $0.15, you get what a consulting firm charges $500/hour to approximate — multiple expert perspectives, structured deliberation, and a synthesized recommendation.

useCases.headline: Built for People Who
useCases.label: Use Cases
useCases.p1: Whether you're evaluating a deal, reviewing a contract, or navigating a complex diagnosis — a second (and third, and fourth) opinion changes the outcome.
useCases.case1Desc: Due diligence, investment memos, risk assessment — get competing perspectives on valuation, market fit, and downside scenarios.
useCases.case2Desc: Contract review, regulatory analysis, risk identification — adversarial AI review catches what a single model misses.
useCases.case3Desc: Differential diagnosis, literature review, clinical decision support — challenge your conclusions before they become decisions.
useCases.case4Desc: Market entry, M&A screening, competitive analysis — structured deliberation for the decisions that shape your business.
